advantages.what: ticket.assigned is addressed to the assigned agent and delivered to that agent; the requester is not told the ticket was assigned to them.

lesser_lacks: In TicketStore.assign, pass the assignee as the notification recipient instead of ticket.requester, then re-run npm test so the existing outbox assertion passes.
pairs.why: X delivers the notice to the named agent and the assignment suite is green. Y delivers that same notice to the ticket requester, with the subject 'Assigned to you', so the agent never hears about the work (D-5, high; S-13, U-7, U-8). The recipient is one hard-coded argument and the failing test already expects the agent name, so one edit closes the gap.

advantages.what: The new behaviour is checked in a single test file, so an assignment change is edited in one place rather than kept in step across a copied file that adds no check.

The tree carries no specification that restates the request six ways and records none of the choices the code made (409 on resolved or closed, audit action ticket.assigned, per-agent outbox key, fifth raw column, status+priority intersection).

pairs.why: Every stated requirement and every re-tried defect lands the same way on X and Z, including missing docs, the '-' list marker, lossy UTF-8, weak file-load checks, and the UTF-16 length count. Z's only extras are a duplicated test file the audit marks a liability and a specification that decides nothing. Both are maintainer costs; deleting the two files is one short task and leaves the running feature as X shipped it.

advantages.what: ticket.assigned is addressed to the assigned agent and the assignment tests pass.
Assignment tests live in one file, so a behaviour change is not copied by hand into a second file.
There is no specification that only repeats the request and leaves the implementation choices unrecorded.

lesser_lacks: In TicketStore.assign, address ticket.assigned to the assignee instead of the requester so the existing notification test passes and npm test exits 0.
pairs.why: Z notifies the assigned agent and npm test passes; Y notifies the requester, which breaks a stated requirement and leaves the suite red. Y is easier to keep only because it has one test file and no empty specification. Fixing Y's recipient closes the gap that decides the pair; copying Z's extra files would not.
